title: “I Heard a Rumour” by Bananarama
text: "I Heard a Rumour" is a song by the English girl group Bananarama from their fourth studio album, Wow!, and was released on 22 June 1987 as the album's lead single.

title: “Don't Mean Nothing” by Richard Marx
text: "Don't Mean Nothing" is the debut single by singer/songwriter/producer Richard Marx from his triple-platinum 1987 self-titled debut album. It hit No.

title: “Songbird” by Kenny G
text: "Songbird" is a song by Kenny G, played on a soprano saxophone, and the third single from his 1986 album Duotones. It reached No.

title: “Carrie” by Europe
text: "Carrie" is a power ballad by the Swedish rock band Europe released in 1987. It was the third single released internationally from the album The Final Countdown and was a Top 30 hit in several territories worldwide.

title: “Don't Disturb This Groove” by The System
text: "Don't Disturb This Groove" is a song by the synthpop/R&B duo The System, from the 1987 album Don't Disturb This Groove. The song was written by the System's David Frank and Mic Murphy.
listen: Don't Disturb This Groove The System

title: “La Isla Bonita” by Madonna
text: "La Isla Bonita" is a song by American singer Madonna from her third studio album, True Blue (1986). Initially composed as an instrumental demo by Patrick Leonard and Bruce Gaitsch, later developed by Madonna, who added lyrics and co-produced it with Leonard.

title: “Bad” by Michael Jackson
text: "Bad" is a song by the American singer Michael Jackson, released by Epic Records on September 7, 1987, as the second single from his album Bad. It was written and composed by Jackson, and produced by Jackson and Quincy Jones.

title: “Sign o' the Times” by Prince
text: "Sign o' the Times" is a song from the American musician Prince's 1987 album of the same name, released as a single on February 18, 1987. The song was intended for two separate Prince studio albums meant to be released in 1986, both shelved: Dream Factory and Crystal Ball.

title: “Change of Heart” by Cyndi Lauper
text: "Change of Heart" is a song by American singer and songwriter Cyndi Lauper, released on November 11, 1986 as the second single from her second album, True Colors. It went gold in the US, peaking at No.

title: “Come Go with Me” by Exposé
text: "Come Go with Me" is a song by American girl group Exposé from their debut studio album Exposure. Composed and produced by Lewis A. Martineé, the song was released in January 1987 as the third single from Exposure.

title: “Can't We Try” by Dan Hill featuring Vonda Shepard
text: "Can't We Try" is a 1987 duet performed by Dan Hill and Vonda Shepard. The ballad was Billboard's No.1 Adult Contemporary Song of the Year for 1987, even though it only reached No.2 on the weekly charts.
listen: Can't We Try Dan Hill featuring Vonda Shepard

title: “To Be a Lover” by Billy Idol
text: "To Be a Lover" is a song written by William Bell and Booker T. Jones, and originally performed by Bell as a soul ballad titled "I Forgot to Be Your Lover". It was released in late 1968, hitting No.
listen: To Be a Lover Billy Idol

title: “Mandolin Rain” by Bruce Hornsby and the Range
text: "Mandolin Rain" is the third track from The Way It Is, the debut album for Bruce Hornsby and the Range. The song was co-written by Bruce Hornsby and his brother John, and featured Range member David Mansfield on the title instrument.
listen: Mandolin Rain Bruce Hornsby and the Range

title: “Breakout” by Swing Out Sister
text: "Breakout" is a song by British band Swing Out Sister. It was released in September 1986 as the second single from their debut album It's Better to Travel.

title: “Stand by Me” by Ben E. King
text: "Stand by Me" is a song originally recorded by American singer-songwriter Ben E. King in 1961, and written by him, along with Jerry Leiber and Mike Stoller, who together used the pseudonym Elmo Glick. According to King, the title is derived from, and was inspired by, a spiritual written by Sam Cooke and J. W. Alexander called "Stand by Me Father", recorded by the Soul Stirrers with Johnnie Taylor singing lead.
wiki: Stand by Me (Ben E. King song)
listen: Stand by Me Ben E. King

title: “Tonight, Tonight, Tonight” by Genesis
text: "Tonight, Tonight, Tonight" is the second track on the 1986 album Invisible Touch by the English rock band Genesis, released in January 1987 as the fourth single from the album. It peaked at No.

title: “Someday” by Glass Tiger
text: "Someday" is a song by Canadian pop band Glass Tiger. It was released on 1986 as the third single from their debut studio album The Thin Red Line through Capitol Records in Canada and Manhattan Records worldwide.

title: “When Smokey Sings” by ABC
text: "When Smokey Sings" is a song by the English pop band ABC, released as the first single from their fourth studio album Alphabet City. The lyrics and title of the song are a tribute to R&B and soul singer Smokey Robinson.

title: “Casanova” by LeVert
text: "Casanova" is a song by American R&B vocal group LeVert, written and produced by Reggie Calloway. Released as a single in 1987, it reached number five on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart and number nine on the UK Singles Chart—LeVert's only top-40 hit on either chart.

title: “Rhythm Is Gonna Get You” by Gloria Estefan and Miami Sound Machine
text: "Rhythm Is Gonna Get You" is a song written by Enrique "Kiki" Garcia and Gloria Estefan, and released by Gloria Estefan and Miami Sound Machine in 1987 as the lead single from their tenth studio album, Let It Loose (reissued internationally as Anything for You). The song was their fourth top 10 (and second top five) single on the US Billboard Hot 100, peaking at number five.
listen: Rhythm Is Gonna Get You Gloria Estefan and Miami Sound Machine

title: “Rock Steady” by The Whispers
text: "Rock Steady" is a song by American group the Whispers, released as a single from their 18th studio album Just Gets Better with Time. Originally recorded as a demo in 1986 by Kenneth "Babyface" Edmonds, he later produced the song along with Antonio "L.A." Reid.

title: “Wanted Dead or Alive” by Bon Jovi
text: "Wanted Dead or Alive" is a power ballad by American band Bon Jovi. It is from their 1986 album Slippery When Wet.
wiki: Wanted Dead or Alive (Bon Jovi song)
listen: Wanted Dead or Alive Bon Jovi

title: “Big Time” by Peter Gabriel
text: "Big Time" is a song by the English rock musician Peter Gabriel from his fifth studio album So. It was his second top-ten single on the US Billboard Hot 100, peaking at no.

title: “The Finer Things” by Steve Winwood
text: "The Finer Things" is a 1987 song written and performed by Steve Winwood. It was released as the fourth single from Winwood's 1986 album Back in the High Life.

title: “Let Me Be the One” by Exposé
text: Let Me Be the One is a single by Exposé, released in 1987. It was written and produced by Lewis Martineé and appears on their debut album, Exposure.
wiki: Let Me Be the One (Exposé song)
listen: Let Me Be the One Exposé

title: “Is This Love” by Survivor
text: "Is This Love" is a song by American rock band Survivor. The song was released on October 1, 1986 as the first single from Survivor's sixth album, When Seconds Count.

title: “Diamonds” by Herb Alpert
text: "Diamonds" is a song by American trumpeter Herb Alpert from his 27th studio album, Keep Your Eye on Me. Released as the second single from Keep Your Eye on Me on March 14, 1987, by A&M Records, the song features lead and background vocals by American singers Janet Jackson and Lisa Keith.

title: “Point of No Return” by Exposé
text: "Point of No Return" is a single by the American pop group Exposé. Written and produced by Lewis Martineé, the single was originally released in 1984 on the Pantera label with Alejandra Lorenzo as the lead singer.

title: The governments of the Portuguese Republic and the People's Republic of China sign an agreement in which Macau will be returned to China in 1999.
text: The Joint Declaration on the Question of Macau, or Sino-Portuguese Joint Declaration, was a treaty between Portugal and the People's Republic of China over the status of Macau. The full name of the treaty is Joint Declaration of the Government of the Portuguese Republic and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the question of Macau.

title: Turkey applied for membership to the European Economic Community (now the European Union).
text: The European Economic Community was a regional organisation created by the Treaty of Rome of 1957, aiming to foster economic integration among its member states. It was subsequently renamed the European Community (EC) upon becoming integrated into the first pillar of the newly formed European Union (EU) in 1993.

title: The Simpsons cartoon first appears as a series of shorts on The Tracey Ullman Show.
text: The Simpsons is an American animated sitcom created by Matt Groening and developed by Groening, James L. Brooks and Sam Simon for the Fox Broadcasting Company. It is a satirical depiction of American life, epitomized by the Simpson family, which consists of Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and Maggie.

title: In Colombo, Sri Lanka, the Central Bus Station Bombing kills 113 civilians.
text: The Colombo central bus station bombing was the car bombing of the central bus terminal of Colombo carried out on April 21, 1987, in Pettah, Colombo, Sri Lanka. The 80-pound bomb killed at least 113 people and left a 10-foot (3 m) crater in the ground.

title: The United States Department of Justice declares incumbent Austrian president Kurt Waldheim an "undesirable alien".
text: Kurt Josef Waldheim was an Austrian politician and diplomat. Waldheim was the secretary-general of the United Nations from 1972 to 1981 and the president of Austria from 1986 to 1992.

title: Canadian Prime Minister Brian Mulroney and the Provincial Premiers agree in principle to the Meech Lake Accord which would bring Quebec into the constitution.
text: Martin Brian Mulroney was a Canadian lawyer, businessman, and politician who served as the 18th prime minister of Canada from 1984 to 1993. He led the Progressive Conservative Party of Canada and served as a member of Parliament (MP) from 1983 to 1993.

title: The U.S. Supreme Court rules in Rotary Int'l v. Rotary Club of Duarte that local Rotary Clubs do not have a constitutional right to deny membership to women. Other clubs thereafter comply with the ruling: Lions International begins…
text: Rotary International is a global service organization, headquartered in Evanston, Illinois, that is one of the largest service organizations in the world. The self-declared mission of Rotary, as stated on its website, is to "provide service to others, promote integrity, and advance world understanding, goodwill, and peace through fellowship of business, professional, and community leaders".

title: Loughgall ambush: A 24-man unit of the British Army Special Air Service (SAS) ambushed eight members of the Provisional Irish Republican Army (IRA) as they mounted an attack on a Royal Ulster Constabulary (RUC) barracks. All IRA members…
text: On 8 May 1987, an eight-man unit of the Provisional Irish Republican Army launched an attack on the Royal Ulster Constabulary (RUC) base in the village of Loughgall, County Armagh, Northern Ireland. An IRA member drove a digger with a bomb in its bucket through the perimeter fence, while the rest of the unit arrived in a van and fired on the building.

title: A Soviet-made Ilyushin Il-62 airliner, operated by LOT Polish Airlines, crashes into a forest just outside Warsaw, killing all 183 people on board.
text: The Ilyushin Il-62 is a Soviet long-range narrow-body jetliner conceived in 1960 by Ilyushin. As a successor to the popular turboprop Il-18 and with capacity for almost 200 passengers and crew, the Il-62 was the world's largest jet airliner when first flown in 1963.

title: Klaus Barbie goes on trial in Lyon for war crimes committed during World War II.
text: Niklaus Barbie was a German officer of the Schutzstaffel and Sicherheitsdienst and a convicted war criminal. He worked in Vichy France during World War II. He became known as the "Butcher of Lyon" for having personally tortured prisoners—primarily Jews and members of the French Resistance—as the head of the Gestapo in Lyon.
